title: Attention and the Construction of Experience
reflection: Three times today, notice where your beam is, and gently take hold of the controls.

questions.q: Why does Conversation 3.5 call attention an active beam and not a passive window?
o: You mostly live what your attention lands on, and it is the factor you can take hold of now.
Attention sees the world exactly as it is, so that nothing at all is ever added by the mind itself.
Attention is fixed at birth, so a person can only learn to live with the beam that they were given.
Attention belongs wholly to the senses, which decide for themselves where they will look and for how long.
questions.e: Like a torch in a dark room, you mostly experience whatever it lands on. You cannot change the world or quickly change your conditioning or noise, but you can aim, brighten and steady your attention now.
questions.c: Attention is the factor you can take hold of directly

questions.q: What are the three trainable controls of attention in Conversation 3.5?
o: Brightness, aim and tuning, and steadiness of timing, each of which can be trained.
Speed, size and colour, which together decide how long a thought will go on ringing.
Sight, sound and touch, which together decide what a person is able to notice at all.
Past, present and future, which together decide where a person places their beam.
questions.e: Brightness is the energy you pour in, from how awake you are plus how much you care. Aim and tuning is where you point and how well your rhythm matches what is there. Steadiness of timing is being truly in step, like pushing a swing at the right moment.
questions.c: Brightness, aim and tuning, steadiness of timing

questions.q: “A beam can be both a narrow spotlight that knows one thing deeply and a wide floodlight that catches every change, at the same time.”
questions.e: A narrow beam knows one thing deeply but is blind to the rest; a wide beam catches any change but knows nothing deeply. You cannot have both at once. Training moves from noticing where the beam goes, to holding it narrow, to holding it narrow and effortless.
questions.c: A beam cannot be both spotlight and floodlight at once

questions.q: A man holds his attention on one point, and it feels like gripping. What does Conversation 3.5 say about this stage?
o: It is the normal first stage: the aim is to hold it narrow and effortless, like oil pouring.
It is a sign that he is doing it wrongly, so he should give up the practice for now.
It is the final stage, since a firm grip is what steady attention means at its best.
It shows that his beam is too wide, so he should open it to take in everything.
questions.e: Holding the beam narrow first feels like gripping. The training continues to holding it narrow and effortless, like oil pouring smoothly. A steady beam also lowers the noise floor; a jumping beam keeps it high.
questions.c: Gripping is the first stage; effortless is the aim

questions.q: A woman is anxious before a meeting, and the evidence that all is well arrives faint. What does Conversation 3.5 suggest?
o: See the forecast as a forecast, and re-aim toward what is present.
Argue with the forecast until she is quite certain that it is false, and only then go ahead.
Feed the forecast with a great deal more detail, since a clear forecast is easier to answer.
Avoid the meeting altogether, since the forecast is what she is really and truly seeing.
questions.e: The mind forecasts what is coming and you experience mostly the forecast, with the senses returning the difference. In anxiety the beam locks onto a threat-forecast. The freeing move is to see the forecast as a forecast and re-aim.
questions.c: See the forecast as a forecast, then re-aim

questions.q: A man with low mood cannot bring himself to re-aim his attention. What does Conversation 3.5 suggest first?
o: Raise the brightness through the body: gentle movement, breath and rest, with proper care.
Concentrate harder on the beam, since more effort is surely the way to move it again at once.
Wait until his mood lifts by itself, and begin any attention work only after that has happened.
Aim at the dark, since a dim beam is the one that shows best exactly what is wrong with him.
questions.e: Low mood is different: the beam is dim as well as locked on a nothing matters forecast, so there is little energy to re-aim. Raise the brightness through the body before attention work can take, always alongside proper care.
questions.c: In low mood, raise the brightness through the body first

questions.q: “Both anxiety and low mood are attention caught in a pattern, and neither is a verdict on the person.”
questions.e: The lesson holds both as patterns of the beam: anxiety with the beam locked on a threat, low mood with the beam dim. They can be worked with, and say nothing final about who a person is.
questions.c: These are patterns of the beam, not verdicts

questions.q: A man has trained his attention to be very steady, but it rests on a story that is false. What does Conversation 3.5 warn?
o: A steady beam on a false story makes him more certain of it, so discernment must walk alongside.
A steady beam is always right, since steadiness is the same thing as seeing the truth.
A steady beam should be loosened, since any steadiness leads to a kind of prison.
A steady beam does not matter, since only the content of a story is of any account.
questions.e: Aim must walk with clear seeing. A steady beam held on a false story only makes you more certain of it. Without discernment, focus becomes a sharper prison.
questions.c: Steadiness without discernment becomes a sharper prison

questions.q: A teenager finds that her beam keeps being pulled by alarms and comparisons on her phone. What does Conversation 3.5 suggest?
o: Notice where the beam is pulled, and take the controls back with less input and a steady practice.
Blame herself, since a strong enough character would never be pulled in this way.
Give up on attention, since the pull of such tools is much too strong for anyone.
Match the pull, since following the beam wherever it goes is the same as freedom.
questions.e: Much technology is engineered to grab attention with novelty, alarm, outrage and comparison. The remedy is the same as for anxiety: notice where the beam is being pulled, and deliberately take the controls back, so you can aim your own light.
questions.c: Notice the pull, and take the controls back

questions.q: “A steady beam lowers the mind’s noise floor, and a jumping beam keeps it high.”
questions.e: A steady beam also lowers the mind’s noise floor. A jumping beam keeps it high, which is one reason why training moves from noticing where the beam goes to holding it steady.
questions.c: A steady beam lowers the noise floor; a jumping one keeps it high
